up.note: Via $\mathrm{rdeg}(f)=\max\{\mathrm{ndeg}(f),\mathrm{ndeg}(\bar f)\}$ and $\mathrm{ndeg}\le\mathrm{C}$. The latter is the sum of the indicators of the minimal $1$-certificates: it is positive on every $1$-input and vanishes on every $0$-input of the domain, because a domain $0$-input consistent with a $1$-certificate would contradict that certificate. Off-domain inputs are unconstrained, so the argument runs unchanged for partial $f$.

facts: Read-once $\mathsf{AC}^0$/$\mathsf{TC}^0$ formulas: $\mathrm{rdeg}(f)=\Omega(\sqrt{\deg(f)})$; with parity gates and depth $d$, $\Omega(\deg(f)^{1/2d})$.
Almost every $f$ on $n$ variables has $\mathrm{rdeg}(f)\ge n/2-O(\sqrt n)$.
$\deg_{\pm}(f)\le 2\,\mathrm{rdeg}(f)$, tight on parity; and $\mathrm{rdeg}(f)=\Omega(\log n)$ for any $f$ depending on all $n$ variables, tight on \(\mathrm{ADDR}_k\) [KKWY26].

Fortnow's question, answered in 2026: $\deg(f)=\widetilde O(\mathrm{rdeg}(f)^3)$ and $\mathrm{D}(f)\le16\,\mathrm{rdeg}(f)^4$ [KKWY26]. The rdeg column of the big matrix read "?" from 1994 until then; what is left is the exponent, see What is the exponent of … versus …?.

self.short: Least d such that f = p/q on the domain with deg(p), deg(q) <= d.

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
